subject: VPC island DNS override, CSR workflow & multi-tier TLS termination
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC island DNS override, CSR workflow & multi-tier TLS termination

Hi Alice and FinBank team,

Thanks for the time on Friday — following up with a concise plan for the private-hosted deployment (your "VPC islands"). Goal: minimize blast radius while giving you ownership of egress/edge TLS and a practical cert rotation model that works for air-gapped segments. Attached is a simple diagram (vpc-island-tls-arch-v1.drawio).

Key proposal (summary):
- DNS: split-horizon / conditional forwarder so internal FQDNs for redwood endpoints resolve to private IPs inside your VPCs; public resolution remains unchanged. We recommend a short TTL (60s-300s) during initial rollout.
- TLS termination: two-tier approach:
  1) Customer edge (your ingress) terminates external client TLS and performs WAF/IP allowlist; it then forwards to an internal edge proxy.
  2) Internal edge proxy <-> Redwood Private connector uses mutual-TLS (mTLS) for authentication and encryption. Redwood will accept certs you provide (offline-signed CSR flow) or integrate with your internal CA via signed certificate uploads.
- CSR workflow: for air-gapped VPCs we prefer an offline CSR approach (you run CSR, sign with your CA, upload PEM to Redwood control plane). For fully managed customers we can optionally support ACME if outbound reachability is available.
- Certificate rotation & ops: 90-day maximum cert validity for edge certs recommended; rotate via staged rollout with canary and automatic fallback. We provide a validation endpoint and health-check hooks to automate cutover.

Asks / open items for your infra team:
1) Confirm whether your internal PKI team will sign CSRs or if you need Redwood to act as intermediary.
2) Provide the thumbprint / public key of the CA we'll trust (attached accepted formats: PEM).
3) Confirm routing: can you create conditional-forwarder rules for the redwood-private.* zone to point at a VPC resolver (IP) per region?

Next steps: if this matches your expectations I propose a 30-min call Tuesday to walk the diagram and the upload flow (we can use the mutual-tls-checklist.pdf as a runbook).

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: VPC island DNS override, CSR workflow & multi-tier TLS termination

Rachel — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) PKI: Our internal PKI team will sign CSRs for internal-facing certs. We do not allow external ACME flows from air-gapped subnets. We can provide the CA cert and fingerprint (attaching finbank-internal-ca.pem).

2) DNS: We can create conditional forwarders to our resolver in each VPC region; however, we would prefer a per-tenant namespace so ops can control delegation without touching global zones. Is redwood-private.{tenant}.finbank.local a supported pattern?

3) mTLS: We like the mTLS path between internal edge proxy and Redwood connector. Two operational asks: a) ability to preregister certificate thumbprints in your console; b) a rotation window capability that allows a 48-hour overlap.

I'll loop in one of our PKI engineers on the call — available Tuesday 11:00–12:30 ET.

Regards,

Alice Jenkins
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, FinBank
alice.jenkins@finbank.com

Subject: Re: VPC island DNS override, CSR workflow & multi-tier TLS termination

Hi Alice — quick technical responses and a recommended implementation sequence.

Implementation sequence (recommended):
1) Zone and FQDN pattern: Use per-tenant subdomains under your private authority, e.g. redwood-private.TENANT.finbank.local. That avoids global zone edits and lets you manage ACLs per-tenant. Redwood accepts arbitrary hostnames — we just need consistent CN/SANs when generating CSRs.

2) DNS mechanics: Configure conditional forwarders from your VPC resolvers to a trusted resolver that we can register in our records, or simply return private A records via your resolver. For cross-VPC reachability please confirm VPC peering/transit gateway rules. TTL guidance: 120s during rollout, increase to 600s for steady state.

3) CSR & offline signing:
- Option A (preferred for air-gapped): You generate a CSR using our template (we'll provide a script). Your PKI signs it and returns cert.pem + chain. You upload cert.pem to the Private control plane.
- Option B: If you want Redwood to handle CSR and initial key escrow, we'd need an approved legal addendum. Not recommended for regulated banks.

4) mTLS details:
- Two-way TLS between internal edge proxy and Redwood connector. We support x509 client cert validation by thumbprint and full chain validation.
- Rotation: we will support a staged rollout window — upload new cert, mark as canary (10% traffic), then promote. If the canary fails we automatically roll back to previous cert. We'll add a 48-hour overlap option to the upload API so both certs are valid during rotation.

5) Healthchecks & validation: Provide a /__redwood/validate endpoint that returns TLS and SAN assertions pre-cutover. We will provide a small agent you can run in a dev VPC to assert connectivity and cert pinning.

Operational notes:
- Keep private keys inside your HSM/HSM-backed CA if possible; we never ask for private keys.
- For air-gapped review, we'll exchange fingerprints and pre-register serials before upload.

I'll attach a short checklist and the script templates on the call. If you confirm Tuesday 11am ET we can send the CSR template ahead of time.

—Karthik
